english: It rained in the morning. It has stopped now.
tip: 그치다 (geuchida) = (rain or snow) stops: 비가 그쳤어요.

english: It is drizzling.
tip: -씩 (-ssik) = bit by bit: 조금씩 = little by little.

english: I got caught in the rain and my clothes got soaked.
tip: 비를 맞다 (bireul matda) = get rained on — you "receive" the rain.

english: There was thunder.
tip: 천둥이 치다 (cheondungi chida) — thunder "strikes" in Korean.

english: A typhoon is coming.
tip: -고 있어요 (-go isseoyo) = is ...ing right now: 오고 있어요 = is coming.

english: A typhoon is coming tomorrow. Please be careful.
tip: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 (-l geoyeyo) = will / is going to: 올 거예요 = it will come.

english: We canceled soccer because of the rain.
tip: Only the last verb takes past tense: 비가 와서 축구를 취소했어요 (biga waseo chukgureul chwisohaesseoyo). 와서 (waseo) stays tense-free even though the rain already happened – -서 never takes 었 (-eot).

english: The first snow fell!
tip: Snow 'comes' in Korean: 첫눈이 왔어요 (cheonnuni wasseoyo = the first snow came). Rain too – 비가 와요 (biga wayo = it rains). There is no single verb 'to snow' or 'to rain'.

english: It is snowing thick and fast outside.
tip: Korean describes how with sound-words: 눈이 펑펑 와요 (nuni peongpeong wayo) – 펑펑 (peongpeong) is fat snowflakes falling thick. Rain pours 주룩주룩 (jurukjuruk).

english: How many degrees is it today?
tip: 몇 도예요? (myeot doyeyo) — degrees ride on Sino numbers: 오 도, 이십 도.

english: I put on gloves.
tip: 끼다 (kkida) = wear things that slide on — gloves, rings, glasses.

english: I put on a scarf and went out.
tip: 목도리를 하다 (mokdorireul hada) — scarves are "done", not worn.

english: The cold has finally eased up.
tip: 날씨가 풀리다 (pullida) — the cold "loosens" when a freeze ends.

english: Spring is here. Flowers have started to bloom.
tip: -기 시작하다 (-gi sijakhada) = start doing: 피기 시작했어요 (pigi sijakhaesseoyo) = started to bloom. The -기 (-gi) turns the verb into a noun the starting attaches to.

english: Wear a mask when you go outside.
tip: -(으)ㄹ 때 (ttae) = when doing: 나갈 때 = when going out.

english: It is hot even at night, so I cannot fall asleep.
tip: 잠이 안 와요 (jami an wayo) — sleep "won't come" = can't fall asleep.

english: I want to go to the ocean in summer.
tip: -고 싶어요 (-go sipeoyo) = want to: 가고 싶어요 = I want to go.

english: The autumn sky is really high.
tip: Koreans praise fall skies as "high": 하늘이 높아요 (haneuri nopayo).

english: In October the leaves turn.
tip: 단풍이 들다 (danpungi deulda) = leaves "take on" their fall colors.

english: Autumn is the season of reading.
tip: Koreans call fall 독서의 계절 (dokseoui gyejeol) — the reading season.

english: Of the four seasons, spring is the shortest.
tip: N 중에서 (jungeseo) = among N: 사계절 중에서 = among the four seasons.

english: A rainbow came out!
tip: 뜨다 (tteuda) = rise, come up: sun, moon, rainbows all 떠요 (tteoyo).

english: In winter the sun sets early.
tip: The sun 지다 (jida = sets) and 뜨다 (tteuda = rises) in Korean: 해가 일찍 져요 (haega iljjik jyeoyo) = the sun sets early. Same verbs work for the moon.

english: My grandmother really feels the cold.
tip: 할머니 is honored: 타세요 (taseyo) — the -시- respect marker on 타다.

english: I suffer badly in the heat.
tip: 더위/추위를 타다 (tada) = "ride" the heat/cold = be sensitive to it.

english: My hobby is hiking.
tip: Answer with noun + 이에요: 제 취미는 등산이에요 (deungsan-ieyo) = my hobby is hiking.

english: I like quiet hobbies.
tip: Descriptive verbs take -ㄴ before nouns: 조용한 취미 (joyonghan chwimi) = a quiet hobby.

english: It's good to have a hobby.
tip: -(으)면 = if: 취미가 있으면 (isseumyeon) = if you have a hobby.

english: Shall we go hiking together next weekend?
tip: -(으)ㄹ까요? = shall we?: 같이 등산할까요? (gachi deungsanhalkkayo?)

english: We drank makgeolli after the hike.
tip: 후에 (hue) = after: 등산 후에 = after hiking — makgeolli is the classic reward.
